rationale: C06 plausibly supplied a material drafting template: both letters seek fiscal-year 1952 supplemental appropriations after Congress eliminated or cut previously requested funds, characterize the original request as the minimum necessary, explain how inadequate funding would cripple the relevant federal program, and conclude by urging full congressional restoration or approval. C03 is also structurally close and concerns the same Independent Offices appropriation process, but it seeks removal of a program limitation rather than transmitting a supplemental estimate. C07 shares the formal appropriation-transmittal frame and minimum-necessary formulation, but less of the child’s restoration-after-cuts structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I have the honor to transmit herewith for the consideration of the Congress, a proposed supplemental appropriation for Fiscal Year 1952
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I am transmitting today supplemental estimates of appropriations for flood control work for the fiscal year 1952.
shared_material.explanation: Both open by transmitting supplemental fiscal-year 1952 appropriation requests.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Approval of this appropriation request would restore funds eliminated by the Congress
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I wish to urge the Congress to restore the funds eliminated by the House of Representatives from the original budget requests
shared_material.explanation: The central legislative request is expressed in closely parallel language: restore previously eliminated budget funds.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The amount involved is the minimum required by the Federal Trade Commission to begin adequate enforcement
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The budget requests included funds for only the minimum necessary work
shared_material.explanation: Both defend the requested appropriation as a minimum operational requirement.

shared_material.child_excerpt: But without funds for enforcement, its constructive purpose will be nullified.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The House action would prevent any of the new projects from being started, would force the suspension of work on some projects now underway, and would seriously delay work
shared_material.explanation: Both develop the same causal argument that congressional cuts would prevent or seriously cripple implementation of an authorized federal program.
